name: G2: Product Details + Reviews
summary: Fetch product metadata and visible-page reviews for a G2 product. Reads schema.org review markup; falls back to og:title/meta tags for product chrome.
description: Open a G2 product page and return product metadata plus a flattened list of reviews. Reads schema.org [itemprop='review'] entries (G2 still ships these) and extracts name/rating/review-count from the page chrome. Pure read.

max_pages.description: How many review pages to walk. Each page yields ~10 reviews. Default 1 (just the landing page); pass 2-5 for deeper coverage.

product_url.description: Full G2 product URL — e.g. the .../products/<slug>/reviews canonical from g2/search. Trailing query strings (?utm=...) and #anchors are stripped automatically.

help.summary: Fetch product metadata and visible-page reviews for a G2 product. Reads schema.org review markup; falls back to og:title/meta tags for product chrome.

parameters.max_pages: How many review pages to walk. Each page yields ~10 reviews. Default 1 (just the landing page); pass 2–5 for deeper coverage.
parameters.product_url: Full G2 product URL — e.g. the .../products/<slug>/reviews canonical from g2/search. Trailing query strings (?utm=...) and #anchors are stripped automatically.

returns: Object: { product: { name, description, rating, review_count, category, url }, reviews: [{ title, body, author, date, rating }], pages_walked }. body is the visible review text after stripping G2's prompt prefixes ('What do you like best...').
notes: G2 ships [itemprop='review'] / [itemprop='reviewBody'] schema markup — selectors target those first; CSS-class fallbacks only kick in if itemprop is missing.
Pagination clicks the pager link on the page, then scrolls and pauses before reading; it never fetches pages in the background. Each extra page adds ~15-25s.
When the walk stops early (max_pages reached or no next link), the result carries stop_workflow/stop_reason next to product/reviews/pages_walked.

Runs for this site queue behind each other and reuse one parked tab, so parallel calls do not speed anything up. If the site shows a captcha or verification wall, the run fails with site_challenge and the site pauses for 15 minutes; solve the challenge by hand in the parked tab.
